name: Voronoi
miniText: How does nearest-site assignment partition space? NetLogo Voronoi places sites and colors every grid patch according to its closest site, producing a raster approximation to a Voronoi diagram. Dragging a site changes the affected territories, which are redrawn outward from the interaction region. Fortune's algorithm [1] establishes the exact geometric construction as a useful comparison; computational geometry [2] explains diagram structure and algorithmic choices; spatial tessellation theory [3] connects nearest-site regions with scientific applications. The NetLogo baseline deliberately uses patch classification rather than calculating exact polygon vertices. Resolution, ties, finite boundaries, and coincident sites therefore matter. The experiment illustrates how a global partition follows from a local distance criterion, while its visual resemblance to cells or territories does not demonstrate any particular biological or urban growth mechanism.
